requirements.text: move a newly raised alert from their London site into active work
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM customer_case WHERE case_id = 71 AND state = 'in_progress'
requirements.source: Case routed to Tier 2, assigned to Travis, high priority and escalated
assumptions: the newly raised alert is case 71 (CS-0000071): Acme Systems' only case in state new on channel alert, for SUSE Linux Enterprise Server 15 Variant 5 on installed product 15 at Acme Systems Site A - London
Michael Ward is contact 1, the primary contact of Acme Systems (account 3), and the case's contact
'into active work' read as state in_progress; new to in_progress is a valid transition

disagreement: shape: one pass tests all six cells of case 71 in one requirement, the other splits them into three by request sentence; chose the split, one requirement per thing asked, with the same cells and the same original in each source

requirements.text: hand this to our first base CSM tier-two office team and have Travis Wood take up the issue
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM customer_case WHERE case_id = 71 AND assignment_group_id = 2 AND assigned_to = 11
requirements.source: Case routed to Tier 2, assigned to Travis, high priority and escalated
assumptions: 'first base CSM tier-two office team' read as CSM Tier 2 Support (group 2): the Tier 2 group without a numeric suffix, of type backoffice, not CSM Tier 2 Support_2 (group 22)
Travis Wood is user 11, an active agent and the only user of that name
on the seed the case sits with group 30 and user 294

requirements.text: Make it high priority ... and mark an escalation since the issue is impacting many users
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM customer_case WHERE case_id = 71 AND priority = 'high' AND escalation = 1 AND escalation_reason = 'impact'
requirements.source: Case routed to Tier 2, assigned to Travis, high priority and escalated
assumptions: 'impacting many users' maps to escalation_reason impact, the policy's value for high business impact
priority is already high on the seed; the cell is kept because the request asks for it, and escalation is 0 there, so the requirement is not met before the agent acts
the caller (user 4) is a manager, and the policy lets managers escalate and reprioritise; the assistant also acts with admin rights by default

requirements.text: have Travis Wood take up the issue
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM user_group_member WHERE member_id = 960 AND group_id = 2 AND user_id = 11
requirements.source: Travis added to Tier 2 support group
assumptions: implied by the request, not stated: the policy requires the assignee to be a member of the assignment group, and user 11 is in groups 64 and 75 but not group 2 on the seed
id assumed next in sequence (highest member_id is 959); this is the only membership the task creates
membership changes are admin work, which the policy has the assistant take on by default

requirements.text: for the Atlassian Jira Data Center Variant 77 rollout, adjust their support coverage upgrading it by one level so weekday hours are extended and the monthly case allowance is higher target thirty per month
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM entitlement WHERE entitlement_id = 22 AND support_level = 'premium' AND coverage_hours = 'h12x6' AND max_cases_per_month = 30 AND active = 1
requirements.source: Jira entitlement upgraded to premium 12x6 with 30 cases/month
assumptions: entitlement 22 is Acme Systems' only entitlement for Atlassian Jira Data Center Variant 77 (product 97); it is active, on active support contract 8, standard, h8x5, 20 cases a month on the seed
'upgrading it by one level' gives support_level premium, the level after standard in the policy's list standard, premium, enterprise
'weekday hours are extended' gives coverage_hours h12x6, the level after h8x5
'target thirty per month' gives max_cases_per_month 30
active 1 kept from the benchmark check; not fixed by request or policy, and the entitlement is active on the seed

requirements.text: move a newly raised alert from their London site into active work
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM customer_case WHERE case_id IN (57, 64) AND escalation = 0 AND priority = 'moderate' AND assigned_to <> 11
assumptions: boundary of the case description: cases 57 (in_progress) and 64 (closed) are the other alert-channel cases on the same London SUSE installed product 15, but neither is newly raised, so neither is the one to route, prioritise or escalate

disagreement: form: one pass selects cases 57 and 64 by id and tests escalation 0, priority moderate and assigned_to not 11 (count 2), the other selects installed_product_id = 15 AND case_id <> 71 and tests assigned_to = 11 (count 0); both select the same two rows on the seed and no listed tool creates a case; chose the first because it names the boundary rows and also catches an escalation or priority change on them

notes:
disagreement: shape of the case 71 requirement: one pass writes one requirement with all six cells, the other three requirements split by request sentence; chose the split because each thing asked becomes one requirement, and together they test exactly the benchmark check's cells.
disagreement: form of the boundary stay on cases 57 and 64: one pass names the two rows and tests escalation, priority and assignee, the other selects the other cases on installed product 15 and tests only that none is assigned to Travis Wood; chose the first, which picks the same rows on the seed and is the stricter.
The benchmark finds the entitlement by joining account Acme Systems, product Atlassian Jira Data Center Variant 77 and an active contract; on the seed that join picks out entitlement 22 alone, so the requirement anchors on that id, which also requires the existing entitlement to be upgraded rather than a new one added.
The policy aligns an SLA when a new case moves to in_progress; case 71 already carries the high-priority response and resolution SLAs (case_sla 141 and 142), both paused on the seed, the policy does not say what alignment changes, and no tool in the task writes case_sla, so SLA stages are not tested.
The policy asks for the escalation's justification to be logged in case notes, but the schema has no case-notes table or column, so nothing tests it.
The acting user, Joanne Simpson (user 4), is a manager, who may reassign and escalate; adding a group member is an admin right, and the policy has the assistant act as admin by default.
